title: Insecure deserialization: the input picks the type
summary: When serialized data names its own .NET type, an attacker picks a class whose setters do something dangerous. BinaryFormatter is gone, Json.NET's TypeNameHandling still bites, and System.Text.Json's polymorphism with an allow-list is the safe way.

steps.title: A message that chooses what it becomes
body: Messages from a queue (or a cookie, or a cache) arrive as:

and the consumer creates whatever type `$type` names. An attacker who can write one message names a different type: one with a setter or constructor that deletes files, starts a process or loads a URL. Such a class is a **gadget**, and big apps and their libraries have many. Chains of them gave remote code execution in Exchange, SharePoint, Jenkins and countless other products.

- **BinaryFormatter** (and `NetDataContractSerializer`, `SoapFormatter`, `LosFormatter`): unsafe by design. **Removed from .NET 9**: its methods now throw `PlatformNotSupportedException`. Old code still runs on .NET Framework, and the unsupported compatibility package brings it back: treat either as a finding.
- **Json.NET** with `TypeNameHandling` set to anything but `None` (`Auto`, `Objects`, `All`) and no strict `SerializationBinder`.
- Hand-written versions of the same idea: `Type.GetType(json["$type"])` and `Activator.CreateInstance`.

steps.prompt: Can the input choose the .NET type that is created?
buckets: No: the type is fixed or allow-listed

steps.title: Polymorphism without trusting the input
body: You often do need "one of several message types". System.Text.Json does it with an **allow-list** written in your code:
var msg = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Message>(json);   // only those two, or a JsonException

The discriminator is a **name you chose** (`order-placed`), not a .NET type name, so the input can only pick from your list. An unknown `kind` is an error, and a missing one on an abstract type is a `NotSupportedException`: catch both and answer `400`.

Also: sign data you must hand to clients and get back (cookies, hidden fields) with an HMAC or ASP.NET Core Data Protection, so it cannot be altered at all (A08 integrity). That is this module's boss.

steps.prompt: A legacy service uses Json.NET with `TypeNameHandling.Auto` for its queue messages and cannot drop it this quarter. What reduces the risk most?
options: A custom ISerializationBinder that allows only the known message types, and rejects every other type name
Validating the JSON with a schema before deserializing
steps.explain: A binder turns "any type" into an allow-list, which is what System.Text.Json's derived types give you by design. Plan the move to `TypeNameHandling.None` anyway.

steps.title: Read queue messages from an allow-list
prompt: `POST /messages` receives messages that say their own .NET type in `$type`. The app also has a `CacheCleanup` class whose `Folder` setter starts a cleanup: a gadget. Fix it with System.Text.Json polymorphism (`using System.Text.Json.Serialization;` at the top):
- `Message` is polymorphic with the discriminator `kind`: `order-placed` → `OrderPlaced`, `order-cancelled` → `OrderCancelled`. Nothing else;
- `POST /messages` deserializes `Message` (web defaults: camelCase) and answers `{ "type": "OrderPlaced", "orderId": 1001 }` (the .NET type name and the id);
- an unknown or missing `kind`, a `$type` message, or broken JSON answers `400`, and never creates a `CacheCleanup`.
`GET /admin/cleanup` shows the last folder a cleanup was started for: it must stay empty.
starter: var type = Type.GetType(typeName) ?? throw new JsonException("unknown type");
return obj is Message m ? Results.Ok(new { type = m.GetType().Name, orderId = m.OrderId }) : Results.BadRequest();
public record OrderCancelled(int OrderId, string Reason) : Message(OrderId);
// Used by the nightly job. Setting Folder starts a cleanup of that folder.
public string Folder { get => LastFolder; set => LastFolder = value; }
solution: return m is null ? Results.BadRequest() : Results.Ok(new { type = m.GetType().Name, orderId = m.OrderId });
catch (Exception e) when (e is JsonException or NotSupportedException)
return Results.BadRequest(new { error = "Unknown or malformed message." });
public record OrderCancelled(int OrderId, string Reason) : Message(OrderId);
// Used by the nightly job. Setting Folder starts a cleanup of that folder.
public string Folder { get => LastFolder; set => LastFolder = value; }
hints: Put `[JsonPolymorphic(TypeDiscriminatorPropertyName = "kind")]` and one `[JsonDerivedType(typeof(OrderPlaced), "order-placed")]` per allowed type on `Message`.
Then `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Message>(json, JsonSerializerOptions.Web)` inside a `try`, and catch `JsonException` and `NotSupportedException` with a 400. Delete the `Type.GetType` line.
template: static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient http, string json) =>
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
await Dojo.TryAsync("Messages could be sent", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("the old $type gadget message gets 400", 400, await Send(http, "{\"$type\":\"CacheCleanup\",\"folder\":\"/srv/data\"}"));
DojoWeb.Status("a kind naming the gadget gets 400", 400, await Send(http, "{\"kind\":\"CacheCleanup\",\"folder\":\"/srv/data\"}"));
DojoWeb.Status("a missing kind gets 400", 400, await Send(http, "{\"orderId\":1}"));
Dojo.Eq("no cleanup was ever started", "", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/admin/cleanup")), "folder"));
